questions.title: What if your ball rolls out of the area two times?
questions.question: You drop your ball, but it rolls out of the marked spot. You drop it again, but it rolls out again. What should you do next?

choices.text: Put the ball down on the spot where it hit the ground after the second drop
Put it anywhere inside the marked spot
Take a penalty and keep playing

questions.explanation: If you drop the ball two times and it won’t stay inside the lines, you should place the ball on the spot where it landed after your second drop.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: The place on the ground where you are allowed to drop your ball, marked by lines or spots.
Letting the ball fall from your knee height so it can bounce and roll.

questions.teachingTip: Use a rope or hoops to show what a relief area looks like, then practice dropping a ball and seeing what happens if it rolls out.
likelyMisconceptions: Some players think you can just keep dropping the ball more than two times.
Some think you can put the ball anywhere in the area after two drops.

questions.title: What do you do if the ball won't stay in the relief area?
questions.question: If you drop the ball twice and it still won’t stay in the relief area, what does the Rule require you to do?

choices.text: Place the ball on the spot where it first touched the ground after the second drop
Place it anywhere in the relief area

questions.explanation: If a dropped ball twice fails to stay within the defined relief area, you must place it on the spot where it touched the ground after the second drop.
